I can’t do web searches from here, and I won’t make up or invent links, citations, or sources. Fabricating sources would be misleading and I can’t comply with that part of your request.

What I can do instead (choose any):

- Explain why the claim “remote work always increases productivity” is misleading and summarize the real evidence landscape up to my 2024 cutoff (some randomized experiments and employer analyses show gains in some contexts, but results are mixed and context-dependent).
- Give you a short list of real, reputable studies/reports (titles + authors/organizations) I’m confident exist and that have documented productivity gains from remote work (with a brief summary of their findings), and show how to find them yourself.
- Produce target search queries and a step-by-step search checklist you can paste into Google Scholar, your library, or a browser to locate primary sources.
- If you can paste or upload links or PDFs you already have, I’ll evaluate and summarize them.

If you want the second option, here are a few real items you can look up (I won’t invent links, but these are accurate titles/authors you can search):

1) Nick Bloom, James Liang, John Roberts, and Zhichun Jenny Ying — “Does Working from Home Work? Evidence from a Chinese Experiment” (Stanford).  
   - Summary: A randomized experiment at a Chinese travel agency found work-from-home participants were about 13% more productive (higher output per hour and more minutes worked), with lower attrition and higher job satisfaction.

2) Nicholas Bloom, Steven J. Davis, and coauthors — NBER working papers on remote work trends (search for Barrero, Bloom, Davis “Why Working From Home Will Stick” and related NBER or working-paper outputs).  
   - Summary: These papers analyze large-survey and employer data about who can work from home and how WFH changed during/after COVID; they document shifts in work location and discuss productivity implications (context-dependent).

3) Major industry/government reports (examples to search): Microsoft “Work Trend Index” reports (2020–2022) and McKinsey “What’s next for remote work” / “The future of work after COVID-19.”
